data.narrative:
Sereact, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Ralf Gulde and Marc Tuscher, has raised $140M to date. The valuation analysis triangulates across a comp universe of nine private peers and one public comparable (277810.KQ), spanning the robotics and manufacturing sector at similar development stages.

Two methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy value base and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, implies $266M. Peer-median valuation across three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—yields a median of $1.8B, with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $226M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.0B. The 8.9x spread between low and high reflects material uncertainty. Stage-progression yields a substantially lower result than peer-median valuation, suggesting either that Sereact's progress exceeds typical stage-advancement patterns or that peer comparables embed sector-specific growth expectations not captured in capital-deployment metrics alone. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the three peer valuations and whether Sereact's operational traction warrants positioning within the peer distribution.
